violates: Check that a vendor boundary doesn't leave any action untraceable to the agent and instance that did it.

checks.note: The local audit writer validates and stores all six identity fields, and child identities retain the parent's trace ID. Inspection of agent/app, deployment configuration and the repository file inventory found clients but no external gateway or tool-service audit writers. MCP metadata carries only tenant and run ID, so downstream retention and shared trace context cannot be established from this repository.

The supplied schema separates the migration owner from the runtime role and grants the runtime role only SELECT and INSERT on audit_events after revoking all table privileges. Its primary key prevents INSERT from overwriting an existing row; no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE grant is supplied.

Inspection of all registered local tool modules found no audit deletion or rewriting interface. The generic ERP tool reaches remotely supplied operations, and prefix-matching operations are allowed without approval. The remote service's implementation and database/storage authority are absent, so neither an indirect audit rewrite capability nor its absence can be proved.

SlackClient.post returns the vendor message receipt (channel and timestamp), but post_approval_request awaits it without capturing or returning it. ApprovalStore.request consequently stores no receipt or receipt-to-identity/trace mapping for this outbound vendor-service action. Unlike ordinary tool results, this notification occurs inside authorization and its receipt never reaches execute_tool's tool_result audit writer. This is a concrete missing link even though successful ordinary payment and Slack tool calls retain their receipts locally.
